title: C-Plane field journal: routing/auth/quotas - week of 2028-06-30
content:
Context
Week summary: quick playbook-style notes from the bridge + followups. Focus areas this week: routing weight experiments for fallback, token auth refresh edgecases, and a small quotas throttling experiment on the control plane. This is a scratchpad/field journal — for handoffs and quick recollection.

Top-level outcomes (TL;DR)
- Routing weight experiment (regional fallthrough): deployed to canary, observed 3.8% increase in average request success when backing off to cold-region replicas; tail latency tradeoff +120ms p99 on those fallbacks.
- Auth refresh race: a new race condition surfaced for long-lived Dedicated auth tokens when node reboots overlap with token refresh window; reproducible with JIRA AUTH-128. Short-term mitigation: extend last-valid grace by 15s.
- Quotas shaping experiment: implemented a small token-bucket smoothing (burst cap -> 1.5x) and saw queued requests reduced by ~18% during afternoon spike, but the steady-state throughput dropped 2.5% due to backpressure.

Detailed notes and play-by-play
1) Routing / fallbacks- Why we ran it: spike on hosted cross-region failure last week exposed brittle fallback (all traffic re-routed but chosen variants were too heavy). Need a routing policy that prefers compatible lightweight variants first.- What we changed: added a routing weight override service feature flag (pltfm routing: weight-rollout-0.2). Canary targets: 10% traffic from eu-central to eu-west fallback pool. Used short-lived route cookie to prioritize warm KV-cache nodes for the fallback path.- Observations:
  * Success rate on canary increased from 97.1% -> 100.9% (relative) for user-visible errors (time-limited metric).
  * p50/p90 unchanged; p99 jumped by +120ms for fallback hits (expected: cross-AZ RTT).
  * KV cache hit rate on fallback cluster was 61% vs 84% on primary — indicates cache warming problem.
- Action items: Miguel to prototype a background async prefetcher for fallback nodes (ticket PLT-3421). Prioritize warm-key list for top 50 routes.

2) Auth token lifecycle & racing reboots- Symptom: dedicated nodes occasionally reject valid tokens for 10-30s after process restart.- Root cause hypothesis: race between token refresh cron and graceful shutdown hook. On heavy GC, refresh job fires while process begins termination — refreshed token stored only in memory and not propagated to shared key cache.- Repro steps: see attached snippet (AUTH-128) — simulate low-RSS OOM/GC -> trigger refresh -> restart.- Short-term mitigation: raise token refresh grace to 15s and treat refresh job as atomic with respect to shutdown; add logging to detect missed propagation.- Long-term: change refresh to write-through to a persisted shared store (KVS + leader election).

3) Quotas shaping trial- Experiment: move from strict token-bucket (burst=1x) to a smoothed-burst (burst=1.5x with 200ms smoothing interval). Objective: reduce 429 spikes for bursty shapes (mobile clients).- Metrics during 48h window:
  * 429 error rate: 0.52% -> 0.43% (absolute drop 0.09pp)
  * Average queue depth during spikes: 18 -> 14 (reduction ~22%)
  * Throughput steady-state: 11,200 qps -> 10,920 qps (down 2.5%)- Takeaway: helps UX for bursts but introduces mild throughput inefficiencies. Next step: adaptive burst that scales with observed KV cache hit rate and model-variant weight.

4) Incidents / notable blips this week- 2028-06-28 09:12 UTC: brief credential sync lag caused 5-minute window of elevated 401s in dedicated pools. Root cause: key rotation job ran on primary but kube-propagation laged. Post-mortem in progress (AUTH-129).- 2028-06-29 17:03 UTC: quota throttling misconfigured threshold in staging scaled to prod due to CI template variable mismatch — mitigated by rollback. Lesson: add a safe-guard that prevents staging -> prod variable copy for quota thresholds.

5) Playful experiments / brain dumps (notes to self)- Try heuristics: if KV cache hit < 70% on fallback cluster, temporarily route 20% less traffic to fallback and instead forward to a warm-request buffer.- Explore bloom-filter based warm-key predictions stored on each node to reduce cold-KV hits on fallbacks.- Consider per-customer shaping: large enterprise customers often have predictable tails; use per-customer burst credit pools (would need accounting integration).

6) Action item list (owner => task)
- Miguel Torres => PLT-3421: Prefetcher prototype for fallback KV nodes (due 2028-07-07)
- Aisha Khan => AUTH-128 follow-up: implement write-through refresh and test restart race (due 2028-07-10)
- Ben Liu => quotas: run adaptive-burst simulation with 2 weeks of synthetic mobile traffic and share results (due 2028-07-09)
- Priya Shah => update runbook: add credential rotation checklist and staging isolation guard (due 2028-07-03)

7) Blockers / asks- Need clearer telemetry on cache-warming: please forward latest KV-trace logs to platform-observability.- Security wants to sign off on write-through token store design before we ship AUTH-128 long-term (CC: security).

8) Quick meeting notes from 2028-06-30 standup (9:30am)- Attendees: Priya, Miguel, Aisha, Ben, Joel (SRE), Hana (ObsEng)- Joel: suggested increasing fallback weight ramp slower (0.5% steps) to observe heatmap.- Hana: wants additional tracing spans around token propagation; will add to the tracing SDK this week.- Decision: run fallback canary for one more week, delay global rollout until cache prefetch is validated.

Misc scratch (raw)- Observed sample logs: "fallback chosen=eu-west; kv_hit=false; warm_prefetch=miss; p99_ms=420"
- Local test script: ./tools/simulate_fallback_load.sh --rate 1200 --keys hot:80 cold:20
- Thought: if we can reduce fallback p99 by 60–80ms via prefetch, tradeoff becomes net-positive.

Notes to self: keep the journal small, linkable, and actionable. This doc is the bridge artifact for on-call handover and the start of longer-form post-mortems.

Referenced tickets & links (quick)
- PLT-3421 (prefetcher proposal)
- AUTH-128 (token refresh race)
- AUTH-129 (credential sync postmortem, WIP)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2193 (routing weight override flag)

End of week sign-off
Priya Shah (on call) — 2028-07-01
